domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's request for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — request created but not yet submitted; employee may edit or cancel
SUBMITTED — request submitted for manager review; employee may withdraw (cancel)
APPROVED — manager granted the leave; balance is deducted; employee may still cancel
REJECTED — manager denied the leave; terminal state
CANCELLED — request withdrawn by employee; can be reached from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED; terminal state

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave is approved or cancelled.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is in effect for the current fiscal year; usedDays and remainingDays are mutable
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays has reached zero; no further leave of this type can be approved
CLOSED — fiscal year ended; balance is frozen and read-only

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Governs how many days an employee is entitled to, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice periods, and accrual/accumulation limits.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; leave requests referencing this policy are processed normally
INACTIVE — policy is disabled; no new leave requests can be created against it; existing balances remain

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type maps to a LeavePolicy that defines its specific rules and entitlements.
lifecycle_states: annual — Annual/paid time off; subject to balance checks, minimum notice, and manager approval
sick — Sick leave; may bypass minimum notice; may require documentation after N consecutive days
emergency — Emergency leave; bypasses minimum notice; may have a separate entitlement or draw from annual pool
unpaid — Unpaid leave; no balance deduction; manager approval required
maternity — Maternity leave; extended entitlement; manager approval required
paternity — Paternity leave; fixed entitlement; manager approval required

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of LeaveRequest lifecycle states. Governs which transitions are valid and which operations are permitted on a request at each stage.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT
SUBMITTED
APPROVED
REJECTED
CANCELLED

business_rules: A LeaveRequest can only transition along these paths: DRAFT → SUBMITTED, DRAFT → CANCELLED, SUBMITTED → APPROVED, SUBMITTED → REJECTED, SUBMITTED → CANCELLED, APPROVED → CANCELLED. REJECTED and CANCELLED are terminal states. No other transitions are valid. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest.status appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays must be incremented by the number of leave days requested, and remainingDays decremented by the same amount. This must happen atomically — approval and balance update succeed or fail together. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest APPROVED transition → LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Before a LeaveRequest can transition to APPROVED, the employee's LeaveBalance.remainingDays for the matching policy must be >= the number of leave days requested. If remainingDays is insufficient, the request must be REJECTED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest APPROVED transition → LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest is submitted, if the associated LeavePolicy has a non-null minimumNoticeDays, the startDate must be at least minimumNoticeDays after the submission date. Emergency and sick leave types bypass this check. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest → LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays appears, not only here]

When an APPROVED LeaveRequest transitions to CANCELLED, the LeaveBalance.usedDays must be decremented by the number of leave days that were originally deducted, and remainingDays incremented by the same amount. This must happen atomically. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest CANCELLED transition → LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Only the employee's manager (Employee.managerId) may approve or reject a LeaveRequest. An employee cannot approve or reject their own request. The actor performing the approve/reject action must match the employee's managerId. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest.approvedBy → Employee.managerId appears, not only here]

If the associated LeavePolicy has requiresManagerApproval set to false, a SUBMITTED LeaveRequest auto-transitions to APPROVED without manager intervention. The approvedBy field is set to null and approvedAt is set to the submission timestamp. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest → LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest can only be created for an employee whose employmentStatus is ACTIVE. Requests for INACTIVE or TERMINATED employees must be rejected at creation time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest → Employee.employmentStatus appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest can only reference a LeavePolicy whose isActive is true. Requests referencing an inactive policy must be rejected at creation time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest → LeavePolicy.isActive appears, not only here]

startDate must be on or before endDate. A request where startDate > endDate is invalid and must be rejected at creation or update time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest.startDate, LeaveRequest.endDate appears, not only here]

remainingDays must always equal totalEntitlement - usedDays. This invariant must hold at all times. Any operation that modifies usedDays must recalculate remainingDays accordingly. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance.remainingDays appears, not only here]

If a LeavePolicy has a non-null accrualRate, the LeaveBalance.totalEntitlement accrues over the fiscal year at that rate rather than being fully available at the start. If maxAccumulation is non-null, totalEntitlement must never exceed it. Accrual is prorated based on time elapsed in the fiscal year. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance → LeavePolicy.accrualRate, LeavePolicy.maxAccumulation appears, not only here]

Every state transition of a LeaveRequest must produce an audit record (per GP-002). The audit record must capture: entityType='LeaveRequest', entityId, action matching the transition (CREATE, SUBMIT, APPROVE, REJECT, CANCEL), oldValues (previous status), newValues (new status), performedBy (actor ID), and performedAt timestamp. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest → AuditLog appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced (for architectureMdUpdate)

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, CLOSED
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE
- **LeaveType** (enum): annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity
- **LeaveRequestStatus** (enum): DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED

## Key cross-entity relationships

- LeaveRequest → Employee (many-to-one via employeeId)
- LeaveRequest → LeavePolicy (many-to-one via leaveTypeId)
- LeaveBalance → Employee (many-to-one via employeeId)
- LeaveBalance → LeavePolicy (many-to-one via policyId)
- LeaveRequest.approvedBy → Employee.managerId (manager approval constraint)
- LeaveRequest.status transitions drive LeaveBalance.usedDays/remainingDays mutations

## Open questions requiring human decision

1. **Leave day counting**: How startDate/endDate translate to a day count (inclusive/exclusive, calendar/business days) — affects every balance and sufficiency rule.
2. **Overlapping leave**: Whether multiple APPROVED requests can overlap in date range.
3. **Emergency leave pool**: Whether emergency leave has its own entitlement or draws from annual.
4. **Sick leave documentation**: Whether a doctor's note is required after N consecutive sick days and how it's enforced.

open_questions.question: How is the number of leave days derived from startDate and endDate? Is the range inclusive of both start and end (days = endDate - startDate + 1), exclusive of end (days = endDate - startDate), or measured in business/calendar days? This affects balance deduction, sufficiency checks, and entitlement comparisons across every LeaveRequest operation.
open_questions.impact: Every business rule that references "number of leave days" — balance deduction on APPROVED, balance restoration on CANCELLED, sufficiency check before approval, and minimumNoticeDays enforcement — depends on this definition. An inconsistent interpretation across call sites would produce the BR-001 anti-pattern.
candidate_options: Calendar days, inclusive of both startDate and endDate (days = endDate - startDate + 1)
Calendar days, exclusive of endDate (days = endDate - startDate)
Business days only (exclude weekends and public holidays)
Business days, inclusive of both start and end

open_questions.question: Can an employee have multiple APPROVED LeaveRequests with overlapping date ranges? If not, should the overlap check be enforced at submission time or at approval time?
open_questions.impact: Affects the approval validation logic. If overlapping approved leave is prohibited, the system must check for date-range conflicts before approving. This also interacts with the balance sufficiency check — two overlapping requests could each individually pass the balance check but together exceed entitlement.
candidate_options: No overlapping APPROVED leave allowed — enforced at approval time
No overlapping APPROVED leave allowed — enforced at submission time
Overlapping leave allowed; only balance check applies
Overlapping leave allowed for different leave types only

open_questions.question: Does emergency leave draw from the annual leave balance, or does it have a separate entitlement pool? If separate, what is the default entitlement and does it reset per fiscal year or per incident?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether emergency leave requires its own LeavePolicy and LeaveBalance records, or whether it shares the annual pool. Affects balance sufficiency checks and the overall leave policy configuration.
candidate_options: Emergency leave draws from annual leave balance (same pool)
Emergency leave has a separate fixed entitlement (e.g., 5 days/year)
Emergency leave is unlimited but requires post-hoc manager approval
Emergency leave has a separate entitlement that resets per incident

open_questions.question: Should sick leave require documentation (e.g., doctor's note) after a certain number of consecutive days? If so, what is the threshold and how is it enforced?
open_questions.impact: Affects the LeaveRequest lifecycle — a new state like PENDING_DOCUMENTATION may be needed, or documentation could be tracked as a separate entity. Also affects approval workflows.
candidate_options: No documentation required for sick leave
Documentation required after 3 consecutive sick days — request enters PENDING_DOCUMENTATION state
Documentation required after N consecutive days where N is configurable per LeavePolicy
Documentation always required for sick leave
